published_prior_art.cite: PennEtAl2025BudgetIV: publishes the nested-budget identified set; DufourTaamouti2005Projection: supplies projection geometry, but neither gives this covariance-aware quota envelope.
PennEtAl2025BudgetIV gives NOME asymptotic confidence sets; SteinerHoussineauSteel2026VIPER gives pointwise finite-sample validity, not this one-event containment of the whole BudgetIV set.
Orlin1993MinCostFlow supplies the generic optimization theorem; the BudgetIV encoding is a useful but routine specialization.
SchlemperMoreira2026WeakIDCS isolates roots for fixed weak-IV statistics, but does not establish an exchange-cycle-complete parametric assignment-envelope inversion.
Fieller1954Ratio supplies scalar quadratic tail classification; no inspected source supplies the nested-quota trimmed-first-stage equality certificate.
Dufour1997Impossibility gives the general locally-almost-unidentified confidence-set impossibility; the quota specialization adds no independent kernel.
Gafarov2025AffineSets treats regular affine identified-set inference; it does not give this quota-envelope endpoint shift, component pairing, and active-tier-label recovery.
LinPanPan2022EggerCoding documents coding dependence in MR-Egger, but the asserted BudgetIV equivariance is a direct sign-action calculation.
Fieller1954Ratio gives the p=1 ratio reduction and WangKang2022WeakIVMR supplies the multi-instrument weak-IV AR context; this is a required reduction, not a new result.
SchlemperMoreira2026WeakIDCS has exact fixed-statistic inversion, but not an auditable equality-complete quota-envelope certificate with polynomial-delay claim.

novelty_flags.label: Proposition 1 (prop:bounded-impossibility)
novelty_flags.one_line: This is an explicitly acknowledged specialization of Dufour's locally-almost-unidentified confidence-set impossibility and should be retained only as supporting context, not a novelty-bearing root result.

soundness_flags.label: Theorem 4 and def:certified-inversion-handle
soundness_flags.one_line: The unconditional bit-arithmetic claim restricts summaries and covariance entries to rational or real-algebraic values but leaves the load-bearing tier thresholds τ unrestricted real numbers, so its boundary polynomials need not have exact-arithmetic coefficients.

soundness_flags.label: Proposition 2 (prop:recoding-equivariance)
soundness_flags.one_line: After simultaneous sign action, invariance follows directly from absolute residuals and covariance conjugation; it is a validation lemma rather than substantive theorem content.

soundness_flags.label: Proposition 3 (prop:all-valid-reduction)
soundness_flags.one_line: The stated K=1, b1=p, τ1=0 reduction is substitution into the definitions plus ordinary denominator clearing, so it is a sanity check rather than an independent result.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: Theorem 2 (thm:whole-set-coverage)
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Exact simultaneous containment is conditional on fixed p and K, independent exact Gaussian blocks, and known positive-definite covariance blocks.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Finite-sample whole-set containment holds only in the stated exact Gaussian subexperiment.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: Theorem 6 (thm:regular-endpoint-limit)
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Endpoint, component, pairing, and label recovery are conditional on the explicitly stated positive-width regular-face domain.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The endpoint limit and label-recovery theorem holds only on the primitive separated regular-face domain.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper gives exact identification from observable covariance statistics and adapts its method to asymptotically valid confidence sets under a common MR assumption.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Section 2.1, Assumptions 1-4 and discussion following them
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper assumes independent exposure/outcome summary associations, Gaussian summary estimates, estimated covariance consistency, and weak-IV asymptotics; its stated inference is asymptotic size control.
The paper gives a necessary-and-sufficient boundedness condition and analytic projection-based confidence-set construction for AR-type confidence sets.
The manuscript develops exact root-finding inversion for polynomial and rational AR/LM statistics and documents grid omissions, but its stated kernel is fixed-statistic weak-IV inversion.

VIPER proves a finite-sample coverage guarantee for calibrated uncertainty intervals when the violation set contains the true value; the available proceedings record describes parameter-wise interval coverage, not simultaneous containment of an identified set.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Summary and equation (16) reference on the primary journal page
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Fieller studies normally distributed estimates and ratio/quadratic-root interval geometry through a quadratic variance inequality.

source_verification_receipts.version: Author-hosted final working-paper text corresponding to Econometrica 65(6), 1997, pp. 1365-1388
source_verification_receipts.locator: Title page publication note; abstract characterization of valid confidence sets for locally almost unidentified parameters
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The published result gives general impossibility characterizations for valid confidence sets in locally almost unidentified parameter problems, covering the substantive kernel of prop:bounded-impossibility.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: State that τ, b, summaries, covariance entries, and q+ are rational or real-algebraic inputs for the unconditional branch; retain arbitrary-real inputs only for the oracle-relative q branch.
Move the recoding and all-valid reductions to validation/sanity lemmas, leaving the complete exchange-cycle inversion and tail certificate as the novelty-bearing root targets.

Add a worked nontrivial p=3, K=2 certificate that explicitly exhibits a cycle-induced optimizer change, equality-tail case, and exhaustive-assignment agreement before claiming the general polynomial-delay theorem.

Compare the completed backend against the published BudgetIV implementation on a prespecified non-NOME summary-data benchmark, reporting component/ray differences and runtime versus exhaustive enumeration.

recommended_next_step: Revise the exact-arithmetic domain and demote the two definitional sanity propositions, then advance the field-level quota-envelope inversion kernel to Stage 0.
